slides.reasoning: Design B delivers the specified condensed futurist numerals, a fuller-bleed rising area chart and a tightly structured metric stack, while Design A leaves a large dead zone at bottom-right and uses generic bold sans with off-palette cyan/red chart dots.

Design B's hand-drawn dashed route, marigold nodes and aubergine footer band deliver the illustrated journey brief with balanced density, whereas Design A is a thin centered timeline with a large empty middle band and a stray tilted clay box.

Design B's ruled enterprise grid, paired before/after panels and clean ROI band read precisely, while Design A's floating boxes, disconnected leader lines and unlabeled circles look diagrammatically sloppy and unbalanced.

Design B integrates the allocation wheel into an orbital map with a labeled $240M core and a disciplined spec table, though its 20% label slightly crowds the ring; Design A is competent but flatter, with a plain donut plus redundant legend percentages and a large empty lower-right.

Design B makes the product the hero with an exploded, annotated render on brushed silver plus a signal-red price bar, whereas Design A relies on a dark generic stock headphone photo that breaks the specified silver-dominant palette.

Design B builds one coherent monospaced chart system with actual-vs-plan curve and a sharply marked activation gap, while Design A's descending regional line is misleading and its 'ACTIVATION'/'TARGET 75%' labels visibly collide.

Design B delivers the requested custom transit-line diagram with interchange bar and a charcoal north-star band, while Design A reduces the pillars to four bar-charts with a large black circle floating awkwardly in dead space.

Design B's week-scaled roadmap with diamond gates, gate callouts, team dot-counts and launch ramp is a genuine program view; Design A is four flat violet blocks with dashed lines and unowned gate captions.

Design B renders an actual continuous loop with satellite annotations, marker-style script and a bottle-green quote panel, while Design A's four circles with disconnected diagonal strokes read as an incomplete diagram with cramped inner text.
Design B's oversized editorial 68% with dot-matrix, app-handover ribbon and blockquote panel is more expressive and better hierarchized than Design A's plain donut and generic circle-arrow chain.

Design B's layered oversized title and structured visible/hidden UI diagram feels like a keynote moment, while Design A leans on generic audience stock photography with a color-band mismatch at the header edge.

Design B organizes the four oversized numbers on one rule with tagged deltas, a white quote card and dark priorities panel, whereas Design A's metrics float unevenly with awkward label alignment and large unused areas.

Design B's illustrated corridor map with kilometre markers, river, scale bar and compass is the informational centerpiece the brief asked for, while Design A's orange dashes floating over a generic tropical photo misread as arbitrary marks.

Design B's baseline-grid letterform with clean leader-line annotations and a comparison column is genuinely instructional, while Design A's rules float unattached to the glyph and labels sit ambiguously far from the forms.

Design B's collage of graphic ingredient forms, aligned metric row, stacked audience bar and peach partnership footer is energetic and structured, while Design A relies on generic catering stock photography with a visible seam and washed overlay panels.
